title: Learning Perceptual Rules in a Fragmented Visual World
summary: Visual perception organizes incomplete sensory evidence into coherent structures, but where do the principles governing this organization come from? We investigate whether learning to predict missing visual information can give rise to structural priors resembling classical Gestalt principles. Masked autoencoders (MAEs) trained on natural images exhibit perceptual completion consistent with good continuation, symmetry, and global form. Critically, when local evidence surrounding a missing region is held constant, manipulating distant elements systematically changes its reconstruction, demonstrating that local predictions are constrained by the global organization of the visual input. We next manipulate visual experience by adapting MAEs to either natural images or texforms that preserve local image statistics while disrupting global spatial organization. This altered experience weakens globally supported completion and shifts perceptual inference toward local continuation when local and global constraints conflict. Together, these results suggest that perceptual organization reflects structural regularities of natural scenes acquired through visual prediction: predictions integrate structural priors across multiple spatial scales, and the balance between local and global organization adapts to the statistical structure of visual experience. More broadly, our findings suggest that classical Gestalt principles may emerge as adaptive perceptual priors learned from the statistical structure of the visual world.

title: RePrior: Measurement-Reconciled Prior Correction for Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction
summary: Sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is severely under-constrained by limited X-ray projections. Learned reconstruction can provide complementary anatomical information, but using it as a prior in patient-specific Gaussian reconstruction introduces two challenges. First, the discrepancy between the learned prior and current reconstruction is spatially non-uniform: some local differences contain useful missing 3D information, whereas others reflect prior bias. Second, even a volumetrically beneficial correction can conflict with the observed X-ray measurements. Since X-ray measurements are line integrals, spatially separated corrections may affect overlapping rays, with their signed projection responses reinforcing or partially canceling in the measurement residual, so their feasibility cannot always be assessed independently. In this paper, we introduce RePrior, a multi-stage progressive prior-correction framework that addresses correction actionability, measurement feasibility, and representation expressivity. Selective Correction Proposal (SCP) first identifies actionable signed local corrections from prior--reconstruction discrepancies. Measurement-Constrained Reconciliation (MCR) then jointly enforces their consistency with patient-specific X-ray measurements, while Hybrid Residual Enhancement (HRE) recovers additional correction capacity through complementary voxel- and Gaussian-domain degrees of freedom around the reconciled anchor. RePrior requires neither test-time ground truth nor case-specific network fine-tuning. RePrior gains approximately 2.6~dB in 3D PSNR over R$^2$-Gaussian across LUNA16, PANORAMA, and PENGWIN. Beyond prior-assisted reconstruction, it delivers additional gains in volumetric quality and observed-view projection fidelity, with consistent gains in held-out-view fidelity in the backbone-matched evaluation.

title: Temporal Diffusion Bridge Model for Vessel Extraction Using Physics-informed Synthetic Data
comment: 13 pages, 6 figures. Under review at Medical Image Analysis
summary: Accurate artery extraction from X-ray coronary angiography (XCA) is essential for coronary artery disease diagnosis and intervention. However, low vessel visibility, respiratory and cardiac motion, and limited annotations challenge existing methods. Moreover, most deep learning approaches produce binary vessel masks without preserving clinically relevant intra-arterial contrast information. We propose a Temporal Diffusion Bridge Model (TDBM) that formulates vessel extraction as image translation and learns from physics-informed synthetic data without manual vessel annotations. A physics-based XCA synthesis engine generates diverse, perfectly aligned pairs of contrast-enhanced and contrast-free images. Using these pairs, TDBM learns cross-domain mappings to recover high-fidelity vessel information. Temporal conditioning incorporates adjacent frames to improve consistency, while a vessel-aware contrastive loss exploits background-invariant synthetic pairs to enhance vascular discrimination. We evaluate TDBM on two XCA vessel segmentation datasets and conduct a reader study using two real-patient XCA sequence datasets. Zero-shot segmentation is further assessed on retinal imaging and fluorescence microscopy datasets. Results demonstrate that TDBM consistently outperforms existing methods and generalizes effectively across imaging modalities. Code and trained weights will be available at: https://github.com/Advanced-AI-in-Medicine-and-Physics-Lab/TDBM

title: Exploring the Latent Structure of AMD Severity Using Retinal Foundation Models
comment: 7 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication at IEEE EMBS BHI 2026
summary: Retinal foundation models have demonstrated strong performance across a wide range of ophthalmic tasks, yet relatively little is known about how disease-related information is represented within their learned embeddings and whether this distribution influences downstream prediction performance. In this work, we use Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) as a case study to investigate how disease severity is represented within the embedding space of RET-CLIP, a retinal vision-language foundation model, using bilateral fundus images from the AREDS dataset, benchmarked against non-retinal encoders. We first characterize the distribution of AMD severity within the learned representation space and then evaluate how this structure influences classification performance across three clinically relevant task formulations of increasing granularity. Finally, we analyze the most influential latent dimensions combining feature attribution, statistical phenotype association, and qualitative image analyses. Our results show that RET-CLIP represents AMD severity as a continuous spectrum rather than a set of discrete categories, with healthy and advanced disease stages exhibiting clearer separation than intermediate ones. This organization was reflected in downstream performance, which decreased from a balanced accuracy of 0.844 and 0.814 for binary AMD and Late-AMD detection respectively to 0.446 for six-class grading. Furthermore, the most influential latent dimensions were statistically associated to distinct retinal phenotypes, including drusen accumulation, pigmentary alterations, and advanced retinal lesions. These findings suggest that the structure of retinal foundation-model representations influences the difficulty of clinically relevant prediction tasks and demonstrate the potential of representation-level analysis for understanding disease organization and improving interpretability.

title: Large-Scale Data Center Integration in Power Systems: Uncertainty and Multi-Scale Variation
comment: Accepted for publication in Proceedings of the IEEE. Copyright 2026 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted. Permission from IEEE must be obtained for all other uses
summary:
Hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) data centers are emerging as a structurally new class of electricity demand. Unlike conventional loads, they materialize as spatially concentrated, transmission-level point loads with rapid deployment timelines and converter-dominated dynamics. Their integration is governed by two defining properties: forecast uncertainty in load realization and multi-scale temporal variation spanning sub-seconds to planning horizons.
  We develop a unified framework that links reliability and affordability to these dimensions through a four-quadrant structure: (reliability, affordability) $\times$ (uncertainty, variation), which integrates probabilistic resource adequacy, generation and transmission expansion, operational security, and market design.
  Measured traces from a public generative-AI workload dataset show strongly tonal GPU power spectra rather than smooth broadband behavior: harmonic combs at the training-step cadence, and a distinct sub-second periodicity in inference. Across these traces the dominant variance band shifts with workload type (seconds for training and offline inference; tens of seconds and longer for online inference). We report this as a characterization of the measured workloads rather than a universal signature, and take it to indicate that such loads warrant a spectral description rather than a peak-demand one. These signatures directly affect reserve requirements, ramping products, voltage stability, ride-through performance, and harmonic interactions in converter-rich grids.
  Taken together, the analytical framework and empirical results establish a system-level basis for assessing the reliability and cost implications of large AI data center integration across planning and operational horizons.

title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Actions Models
summary: The rise of large language models (LLMs) has opened a path toward generalist embodied AI, raising the question of how LLMs can act in the physical world. One straightforward approach is training the model to generate actions: collect robot-action data and video demonstration, refine LLM architecture with an action head, and train a vision-language-action (VLA) model at scale. However, we argue that coding agents have the potential to realize generalist embodied manipulation. All they need is a simple yet effective robot harness. We present RoboHarness: a robotic harness that gives LLM agents a visual-geometric control panel so that they can directly understand and invoke embodied tasks. With RoboHarness, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next outperforms state-of-the-art VLA models on BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025 tasks. The implementation will be released as open source.

title: How Vision Transformers Represent Position: A Mechanistic Comparison of Absolute and Rotary Positional Encodings
summary: Positional embeddings encode the spatial position of each image patch in a Vision Transformer (ViT), allowing the model to distinguish different spatial arrangements of visual content. However, we know little about how the choice of embedding shapes a vision transformer's internal representation. In this work, we show that Absolute Positional Embeddings (APE) and Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE) encode spatial position through different internal mechanisms: APE stores position in explicit features, while RoPE builds it inside attention and rebuilds it when it is withheld. Specifically, in APE models, sparse autoencoders recover causal row- and column-specific features, whereas interventions on RoPE reveal distinct rotary components that separately encode row and column information. Additionally, causal interventions selectively disabling RoPE's row or column rotations show that decodable row and column information can be independently removed and, once rotations are restored, partly reconstructed, in part by axis-specialized attention heads. Both mechanisms are causally important for classification: permuting APE's positional features across patches reduces top-1 accuracy by 24--31 points, and ablating the rotations of RoPE's primary rebuilding head reduces it more than ablating those of any other head. Our findings show that the choice of positional encoding fundamentally changes how spatial information is organized and processed inside Vision Transformers. More broadly, our work demonstrates how mechanistic analysis can reveal how models construct, reconstruct, and maintain structured representations, providing a basis for targeted interventions in vision models.

title: PsyBer-Agent: A Psychology-Driven User Agent for Recommender Systems
summary: Evaluating recommender systems before deployment requires simulators that remain realistic over long, closed-loop interaction cycles. Current LLM-based agents generally function as surface imitators that generate realistic short-term responses but fail to capture the underlying user dynamics such as fatigue, affect, and shifting preferences. We propose PsyBer-Agent, a psychology-inspired simulator that models these dynamics through its Psy-Engine. This engine represents each user with three evolving, model-defined latent states. To calibrate simulated behavior against real interaction logs, we align log-conditioned reference trajectories with simulator-generated latent-state trajectories via Unbalanced Gromov--Wasserstein optimal transport. This approach provides structured supervision for a lightweight policy without the computational burden of fine-tuning the backbone LLM. We also introduce WebSim and the PsyBer Benchmark, which encompass multimodal scenarios and seven recommender backbones. Our framework evaluates behavioral fidelity, latent-state consistency, robustness, and responses to social-cue perturbations. On the tested horizons, PsyBer-Agent shows lower behavioral discrepancy than the prompt-only simulators while maintaining stable performance under large-scale concurrent simulation for up to 5M queued simulation tasks under bounded concurrency. Code is available in the supplementary material and at: PsyBer-Agent: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CC66F/, WebSim Platform: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/D8EAX/.

title: Frozen Site-Probe Accuracy Is Not a Standalone Harmonization Score: An Audit of Evaluation Practice for Multi-Site MRI
comment: 4 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027. Code and results: https://github.com/muqsitamir/HarmonIt. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
summary: Image-level MRI harmonization is often evaluated with a frozen site probe, a site classifier trained on raw scans and applied unchanged to harmonized ones: a drop in its accuracy is read as removal of site effects. We audit this practice on ABIDE I (1,112 T1-weighted scans, 17 sites) with ten output sets from seven harmonization methods and controls for chance, head shape, intensity, preprocessing and target alignment. We find that this verdict depends on how the probe is trained, even among probes that classify raw scans well: across random seeds, its balanced accuracy on the same CycleGAN outputs ranges from 0.13 to 0.59 (chance: 0.06). Low frozen-probe accuracy can also arise without harmonization: a Gaussian blur, which increases the intensity distance to the target site, lowers this accuracy to chance. Moreover, where the frozen probe fails, probes trained on the harmonized scans still recover the site, even from intensity histograms alone: on HACA3 outputs, the frozen probe scores 0.25, a probe trained on those outputs 0.75, and one using only their intensity histograms 0.71. Low frozen-probe accuracy therefore does not show that site information has been removed. We recommend reporting several probes trained to convergence, probes trained on harmonized scans, and target alignment.

title: Zero-Crossing Time Lower Bounds for the Homogeneous Super-Twisting Algorithm
summary: High-frequency switching and chattering are well-known problems in sliding-mode control. Although the super-twisting algorithm produces a continuous control input, the sliding variable may still cross zero repeatedly near the sliding manifold. This paper studies how fast these crossings can occur and whether they can accumulate in finite time for the scalar homogeneous super-twisting algorithm. Two lower bounds on the time required to return to zero are derived, together with a bound on the time needed to complete a full excursion. These results give minimum separation times and upper bounds on the number of crossings associated with excursions above a prescribed amplitude. Although zero crossings may accumulate in finite time, the amplitudes of the complete excursions considered here must vanish and satisfy a summability condition. Thus, crossings associated with excursions above any prescribed nonzero amplitude cannot accumulate in finite time. When the perturbation-rate bound is zero, the estimates recover the scaling imposed by homogeneity. For the classical super-twisting algorithm, the square-root scaling also holds for nonzero perturbation-rate bounds. Numerical simulations illustrate the results.

title: LabInstruct: Benchmarking Situated Instructional Video Generation for Lab Procedures
summary: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) aim to automate the full experimental loop, from scientific decision-making to physical execution. Ideally, AI-generated plans could be carried out directly by robotic systems, but reliable automation remains difficult in complex, open-world laboratory environments, where experiments often involve fine-grained manipulation, long-horizon procedures, and substantial variation across tasks and setups. Humans therefore remain an important execution interface between AI-generated plans and physical experiments, creating a need for clear and effective human-facing experimental guidance. Because laboratory procedures are inherently visual, spatial, and dynamic, video is particularly well suited to communicating apparatus configurations, manipulation actions, temporal dependencies, and state changes. Recent advances in video generation now make it possible to synthesize experimental demonstrations directly from an initial workspace image and a natural-language instruction. However, whether such models can reliably communicate real laboratory procedures has not been systematically studied. We introduce LabInstruct, a benchmark for situated instructional video generation in real laboratories. LabInstruct contains 204 tasks across 5 scientific disciplines, with real reference executions and structured annotations of objects, actions, contacts, and state transitions. Evaluating 8 frontier image-to-video models, we find that visually plausible generations frequently remain procedurally incorrect, revealing a substantial gap between visual realism and the reliability required for experimental instruction.

title: SharedSAE: a unified sparse dictionary across u-net blocks and denoising time for diffusion models
summary: Concept representations in diffusion models drift across network depth and denoising time, yet existing sparse autoencoders offer only per-block or per-timestep dictionaries, leaving no single feature dictionary for localization and intervention in the network. We present Shared Sparse Autoencoder (SharedSAE), which learns one sparse dictionary shared across four U-Net attention blocks and all 50 denoising steps of SDXL 1.0. A block-specific low-rank input adapter aligns the residual distribution of each block before the shared encoder, and a temporal conditioning module with a shared timestep branch and a block-timestep correction branch absorbs temporal non-stationarity. Despite spanning both axes, Shared SAE preserves a coherent dictionary structure. Built on the shared dictionary, localized feature suppression reduces the number of NudeNet-positive generations in the I2P detector-positive subset from 139 to 1. Tracing sparse features across the trajectory further reveals that concept representations are redistributed across U-Net blocks during generation, shifting from the earliest downsampling block toward intermediate and later blocks as denoising proceeds. SharedSAE thus provides a unified, interpretable, and intervention-ready representation space for diffusion models, enabling concept analysis and erasure at any covered block and denoising step.

title: Loose Lips: Understanding Privacy Leakage in Agentic Dialogue
summary: As LLM agents are increasingly deployed in high-stakes enterprise settings, understanding how they handle sensitive information in agentic dialogue has become critical. Privacy leakage in such settings requires reasoning about whether information flows respect the contextual norms under which they originated. We extend CIMemories to CIMEMORIES DIALOGUE, a benchmark of 4,410 two-agent dialogue instances grounded in Contextual Integrity theory. Using this benchmark, we systematically evaluate 7 open-weight models from the Qwen3 and Llama 3.1 families across conversation lengths of 1 and 6 turns under three prompting conditions. We find that task capability and privacy leakage are fundamentally coupled: more capable models are systematically leakier, with no model in our evaluation able to decouple the two. Thinking models consistently leak more than their non-thinking counterparts, a pattern we attribute to the extended reasoning surface created by chain-of-thought. Leakage compounds with conversation length, rising up to 3x from 1 to 6 turns. Our results suggest that the coupling between task capability and privacy leakage is not an artifact of misconfiguration but a structural feature of current agentic systems.

title: C$^2$LUE: Clinically Aligned Patient-Level Ultrasound Diagnosis via Evidence-Aware Multi-Instance Learning
summary: Patient-level ultrasound diagnosis demands not only high predictive accuracy but also clinically aligned mitigation of asymmetric diagnostic risks. While Multi-Instance Learning (MIL) effectively models routine multi-view exams, standard aggregators often dilute heterogeneous diagnostic cues and optimize solely for global accuracy. This frequently yields undesirable sensitivity-specificity trade-offs. To bridge this gap, we propose C$^2$LUE, a novel MIL framework coupling evidence aware aggregation with risk-aligned regularization. To preserve evidence heterogeneity and prevent unimodal attention collapse, C$^2$LUE employs a multi-query cross-attention mechanism built upon a LoRA-adapted DINOv3 backbone. Multiple latent queries explicitly extract and disentangle diverse morphological patterns from the ultrasound sequence. Furthermore, to improve clinical risk alignment, we introduce a dynamic trade-off regularization objective that penalizes sensitivity-specificity imbalance during training. Rather than leaving the clinical trade-off entirely to post-hoc threshold adjustment, this objective encourages the learned score distribution toward a more balanced operating region. Extensive evaluations on patient-level, biopsy-proven thyroid and breast ultrasound datasets demonstrate that C$^2$LUE consistently outperforms prior alternatives. By uniting strong discrimination with a balanced error profile, C$^2$LUE provides a promising solution for real-world ultrasound screening and diagnosis.

title: Deep learning from a control vantage point
summary: This article offers an overview of recent developments in deep learning from a control vantage point. It reviews several classes of models including feedforward and residual neural networks, transformers, large-language models, and selective state space models while explaining how control theory plays an important role in understanding their training, properties, or architecture design. The article explains how residual neural networks can be interpreted as the discretization of a continuous-time control system thereby enabling the use of control theoretic techniques for its analysis. To illustrate the power of this bridge between control and deep learning, two technical results are discussed: 1) the ability of a residual neural network to approximate arbitrary continuous functions is a non-standard controllability problem that can be solved using geometric nonlinear control and 2) transformers, the key architectural component of most large language-models, can be seen the discretization of a consensus algorithm and thus large language-models exhibit consensus. Another point of contact between control theory and deep learning is the connection between backpropagation, the algorithm used to train neural networks, and optimal control. The article addresses how the older connection between these problems, established in the 80's using discrete-time models can be reconciled with the more recent approach using continuous-time models. Several open problems and directions for future research are discussed, including selective state-space models, a recent class of models inspired by the models used in control.

title: OIL: An Object Interaction Layer for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
summary: Recent progress in learned whole-body controllers for humanoid robots has enabled robust free-space motion by tracking kinematic targets such as joint or end-effector trajectories. This interface provides a useful abstraction for upstream systems, including motion capture, teleoperation, or generative models, which can specify desired motion without reasoning about forces or balance. However, this abstraction has largely been limited to robot motion, requiring task-specific controllers or retraining for object interaction. We introduce OIL, an Object Interaction Layer that extends the kinematic command interface of whole-body control to include desired object motion and contact. OIL augments a standard controller with object-centric commands and translates them into coordinated whole-body behavior while preserving locomotion and balance. This design enables a single learned policy to execute non-prehensile interactions, including pushing, pulling, two-arm pick-and-place, and locomotion-coupled transport, directly from object-level kinematic targets without task-specific retraining. In simulation, we demonstrate that object-level commands improve performance over robot-centric controllers while matching task-specific policies across variations in object properties such as mass and size. We further demonstrate zero-shot generalization to novel behavior combinations and sim-to-real transfer on the Digit humanoid robot.

title: Pristine Models
summary: Training on broad, unfiltered data enables high-quality image generation, but can also teach models concepts that should not be generated; restricting the training data ensures safety, but reduces quality because examples containing unsafe concepts also provide useful knowledge that is not itself unsafe. Existing approaches largely address this trade-off post hoc through concept unlearning, which can lead to catastrophic forgetting as the number of concepts to remove grows. We instead ask whether unsafe concept knowledge can be compartmentalized during pretraining so that access to it can be disabled at inference. We introduce Pristine Models, a novel text-to-image generation architecture with an attention mechanism that encourages the separation of safe and unsafe knowledge into independently parameterized branches. The branch-specific parameters are learned during training, while the unsafe branch can be detached at inference. On ImageNet, Pristine Models enable safer generation while retaining much of the utility of full-data pretraining, achieving higher image quality and better text alignment than training only on safe data or applying post-hoc concept removal. We further scale our approach to CC12M, demonstrating that it remains effective in a substantially larger and more diverse open-world pretraining setting.

title: Is the Future Predictable? Modeling Future Predictability for Reliable Temporal Reasoning
summary: Large language models (LLMs) remain unreliable when reasoning about the future. Existing models often overlook the difference among future states, committing to specific answers even when the queried facts are inherently volatile. To capture this challenge, we introduce ChronoRegime, a future-oriented temporal reasoning task that requires models to determine whether historical temporal evidence justifies commitment to a future answer. Furthermore, we propose Confidence-Aware Temporal Reasoning (CTR), a framework that estimates future predictability from temporal dynamics and regulates answer commitment accordingly. Rather than performing unconditional forecasting, CTR commits only when the reconstructed evidence supports the target future state. Across multiple LLMs, CTR improves strict overall accuracy by 6.7 percentage points and reduces hallucination rates by 18.4 percentage points on average over the plain QA baseline. These results demonstrate that explicit predictability assessment is an effective mechanism for safer and more reliable temporal reasoning under future uncertainty.

title: Beyond Discrimination: Evaluating Probability Calibration in Radiomics-Image Fusion for Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification
comment: 12 pages. 1 figure. Accepted at the 2026 Irish Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Cognitive Science (AICS 2026). Proceedings forthcoming
summary: Reliable probability estimates are important for the clinical interpretation of machine-learning classifiers, yet radiomics--image fusion models for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) are commonly evaluated primarily by discrimination. Using 396 patients from the KiTS23 dataset, we evaluated whether adding radiomics to four image-model families improved probabilistic performance in addition to discrimination. Seventeen individual models and four probability-average ensembles were assessed using discrimination, probability calibration, and proper scoring measures. Across 12 matched image-only versus fusion comparisons, AUC and AP improved in all 12, while Brier score and negative log likelihood (NLL) improved in 11 of 12 and expected calibration error (ECE) in eight of 12. The 3D MedVAE gated-fusion model achieved the strongest overall individual-model profile. Probability averaging across concatenation, cross-attention, and gated fusion produced favourable point estimates across all five primary metrics relative to image-only models in all four families, although paired-bootstrap support was stronger for Brier score and NLL than for ECE. These findings show that radiomics--image fusion can improve probabilistic prediction quality beyond discrimination, while calibration behaviour varies across image architectures and fusion strategies. We show that our proposed probability-average ensemble models improve discrimination and calibration simultaneously across all architectures in the study.

title: Spatial-Temporal Hybrid Path Planning for Multi-UAV Methane Emission Rate Quantification
summary: Accurate emission-rate quantification of methane point sources is essential for inventory verification and leak detection. UAV-borne sensing provides high-resolution, near-source measurements, but existing quantification methods mostly follow a predefined trajectory and rely on a single UAV. Building on a source receptor matrix (SRM) estimator and empirical observability Gramian (EMGR)-based path planning, this paper proposes a spatial-temporal hybrid path planning strategy for multi-UAV methane emission rate quantification. Measurements are time-averaged, and the forward Gaussian plume model is calibrated against a filament-based plume simulator (MOABS) to reduce model mismatch. Cooperating UAVs first spread out spatially to locate the source quickly, then switch to sequentially retracing a leader trajectory with a time lag to reduce quantification variance. Simulations show that the spatial stage localizes the source markedly faster than a single-UAV baseline, the temporal stage yields the lowest variance but converges slowly, and the proposed hybrid strategy converges substantially faster than the purely temporal strategy while matching its steady-state accuracy, with a narrower error band than the purely spatial strategy. A window-length study further shows that longer time-averaging windows exhibit diminishing returns, justifying the balance between spatial coverage and temporal averaging.

title: Building Trustworthy Household Robots through Open-World Safety
summary:
Foundation models are expanding robot capabilities, enabling robots to handle more diverse objects, follow sophisticated instructions, and operate in complex environments. These advances bring us to a future in which robots become part of everyday household life. However, cluttered, dynamic household environments also expose robots to unfamiliar objects, tasks, and interactions, making reliable zero-shot task completion an ongoing challenge for robotics research.
  From a security perspective, we argue for open-world safety: household robots should preserve specified safety requirements in unseen situations, including when they cannot complete the requested task. Safety protections must account for context and interactions that persist across actions and tasks. In this position paper, we examine why existing safety methods can fail to provide this protection. Protection can fail through misinterpreted context, overlooked past interactions, or stopping and recovery strategies that become unsafe under unfamiliar conditions. We therefore propose a research agenda to specify, learn, and ground safety requirements, enforce them with reliable recovery, and evaluate the generalization of such protections. We call for household robots whose safety protections remain reliable beyond the situations, context, and history used to train and develop them, to achieve open-world safety.

title: Human Pose Estimation by Probabilistic Mixtures of Gaussian and Uniform Distributions
comment: 38 pages, 11 figures, 20 tables. Includes supplementary material. Code available at https://github.com/santiago-git19/probabilistic-pose-gmm
summary: Despite advancements in sub-pixel decoding, modern Human Pose Estimation (HPE) architectures remain constrained by deterministic coordinate extraction from discrete heatmaps, which systematically fails under dense occlusions and Out-of-Distribution (OoD) ambiguities. To address these limitations, we propose a post-hoc continuous probabilistic framework that intercepts raw heatmaps and models them as a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) augmented with a spatially agnostic uniform distribution, requiring no architectural modifications or retraining. This continuous representation allows us to comprehensively explore the distinct contributions of density modeling to HPE. We show that the spatial expectation of our fitted GMM achieves precision parity with leading sub-pixel decoders without heuristic post-processing. Leveraging this continuous space, our test-time augmentation aggregates probability distributions rather than discrete activations, mitigating multi-scale heatmap poisoning. Furthermore, because our multimodal GMM parameterization isolates competing spatial hypotheses, it naturally interfaces with geometric regularizers such as Markov Random Fields. However, our analysis exposes the inherent vulnerabilities of 2D kinematic priors under perspective foreshortening and visual degradation. Crucially, this density formulation yields significant improvements in uncertainty quantification: our calibrated geometric covariance volume outperforms standard peak-intensity heuristics in OoD anomaly detection under severe occlusion. For in-distribution calibration, dynamically fusing our geometric metric via Adaptive Softmax reduces or matches baseline Area Under the Sparsification Error (AUSE) across benchmarks and degradation levels. Finally, we establish that this continuous parameterization is extensible to multi-view 3D architectures, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$ voxel memory bottleneck.

title: Fin_Agent at FinEval 2026: Task-Aware Methods for Multilingual Financial NLP
comment: 5 pages, 1 Figure, FinEval 2026: Multilingual Financial Language Understanding, Co-located with EMNLP WORKSHOP, OCT 28 2026, BUDAPEST, HUNGARY
summary: We present Fin_Agent, our submission to the FinEval 2026 shared task on multilingual fi nancial language understanding. Our sys tems address Greek financial named-entity recognition, Japanese implicit communication recognition, and multilingual financial ques tion answering. For Greek NER, we com bine annotation-aware numeric rules with zero shot Qwen2.5-32B classification, achieving 0.9521 public F1 and 0.8884 private F1. For Japanese implicit communication, an inter pretable cue-based ordinal scorer achieves 98.0% test accuracy. For multilingual financial QA, BGE-M3retrieval with Qwen3-32B gen eration achieves 0.3023 and 0.3419 ROUGE-1 F1 on the public and private splits. Key limita tions include dataset-specific rules, handcrafted cues, and limited supervision. Implementa tion code is available https://github.com/ Rashidnira/finagent-fineval-2026.

title: Beyond Gate Weights: Decision-Level Interpretation of Radiomics-Image Feature Fusion for RCC Classification
comment: 12 pages, 1 figure. Accepted at the 2026 Irish Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Cognitive Science (AICS 2026). Proceedings forthcoming
summary: Gate coefficients describe how a fusion layer weights intermediate features, but they do not necessarily reflect the magnitude of branch contributions at the classifier output. We investigate this distinction in a fixed 3D MedVAE--radiomics model for clear cell versus non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma classification from contrast-enhanced CT. Because the model uses a linear classification head, the binary decision logit can be decomposed exactly into a gated image term, a direct radiomics term, and a bias. We define effective radiomics dominance as the direct radiomics term's share of the summed absolute non-bias branch contributions and compare it with structural radiomics weighting. Internally, mean structural radiomics weighting was 0.823, whereas mean effective radiomics dominance was 0.148, with a modest case-wise association (\r{ho} = 0.290). The gated image term retained substantially stronger discriminative ranking information than the direct radiomics term. The same structural-to-effective discrepancy was observed in exploratory external evaluation. Branch-targeted permutation, integrated-gradient, and Shapley-style analyses further identified radiomics descriptors influencing the direct radiomics term. Because radiomics also generates the gate, the gated image term remains radiomics-dependent, so additive branch contribution should not be interpreted as total input influence. These findings show that structural gate weighting and decision-level branch contribution represent distinct aspects of gated feature fusion and should be interpreted separately.

title: Encrypted collision avoidance maneuver via variational optimization
comment: 15 pages, 1 figure, extended abstract submited to AAS/AIAA Space Flight Mechanics Meeting
summary: We propose an encrypted collision avoidance maneuver (CAM) design protocol using homomorphic encryption (HE) that enables operators to outsource CAM design to an untrusted server without revealing their private covariance. To this end, we reformulate the constrained CAM optimization as a sampling based estimation problem via a variational approach, so that the private covariance dependent terms can be efficiently evaluated under HE. The protocol requires only a single round of communication, and experiments on six real-world conjunction data messages demonstrate improved feasibility and reduced fuel consumption compared with CAMs designed using public covariance.

title: Residual Compliant Policy: Learning Compliant Policies from Few Demonstrations
summary: Contact-rich manipulation requires a robot to be precise in free space to establish the intended contacts, and compliant once in contact to avoid excessive forces. Imitation learning has proven effective for simpler manipulation tasks, but the compliance underlying a demonstration is not directly observable and is therefore difficult to infer from demonstration data alone. We present a framework that makes compliance explicit at every stage. During data collection, the operator teleoperates the real robot while a synchronized digital twin visualizes the error between the commanded reference and the achieved pose, making the current compliance visible, and selects between two discrete compliance modes. To generalize across object poses, we combine Laplacian editing, which retargets trajectories efficiently but is not physics-consistent during contact, with simulation-based trajectory optimization, which enforces physical plausibility but offers no manual guidance. Finally, a residual reinforcement learning policy refines the interaction forces by adjusting the reference pose of the underlying admittance controller. We evaluate on three flipping and pushing tasks on a Franka FR3 based on a total of 7 demonstrations across tasks. Our method is successful on all 40 out-of-distribution trials, compared to 33/40 and 24/40 for two baselines, with our base policy alone reaching 35/40.

title: Scenes as an Attack Surface: Uncovering Scene-Grounded Safety Failures in MLLMs
summary: Existing jailbreak attacks have exposed serious safety weaknesses in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Most prior attacks rely on specially constructed visual inputs to carry or support harmful intent. In this paper, we uncover a different vulnerability: task-relevant scene semantics alone can shift an MLLM from refusal to compliance, even when the visual input introduces no additional attack instructions and the original task intent remains unchanged. We formalize this failure as a scene-grounded visual safety vulnerability and introduce SceneSafetyBench to investigate it across eight risk categories and nine white- and black-box MLLMs. Our analysis reveals that this failure is associated with how task-relevant visual evidence influences downstream safety representations, suggesting that visual grounding alone cannot fully explain the observed safety shift. Building on this finding, we propose Scene-Grounded Attacks (SGA), which preserve the original task while constructing validated scene-grounded queries and combining their independent responses. Across nine target MLLMs, SGA achieves an average attack success rate (ASR) of 86.17%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 8.55 percentage points and achieving the highest ASR on eight models. Our results identify scene semantics as an overlooked attack surface in MLLMs and highlight a growing tension between stronger visual grounding and robust multimodal safety alignment.

title: Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, 8 tables. Pre-registered study; code, pre-registration and all predictions: https://github.com/tnromy/evaluating-system-one-models-for-indonesian-regional-languages
summary: Calibrated typed-decision ("System One") models return a label and a probability in a single forward pass at a small fraction of the cost of large language models (LLMs), yet their evaluation has been almost entirely English. We report a pre-registered evaluation of the commercial Jev model and the open Laya-multilingual model on Indonesian regional languages, using the parallel NusaX sentiment (12 languages) and NusaTranslation sentiment and emotion (7 languages) test sets. Jev is more often correct on sentences that are lexically closer to Indonesian in all three datasets, and presenting the human Indonesian translation instead raises its accuracy by up to 37.2 points, most in languages distant from Indonesian. Its expected calibration error does not grow on regional languages, but its ability to rank its own errors degrades in all three datasets. Retrained classifiers need more than 500 labels per language to match zero-shot Jev in 9 of 10 NusaX regional languages. A confidence-gated cascade that sends Jev's 10-30% least confident decisions to a local IndoBERT classifier matches or exceeds the better of the two systems, and routing to an LLM instead matches that LLM at 24-77% lower API cost. Of six further commercial LLMs (three Claude and three GPT models), five are 4-14 points more accurate than Jev, at several hundred times the API cost where it is reported, while the smallest (Claude Haiku) is less accurate. We release the pre-registration, code and all predictions.

title: Generative Quantum Machine Learning Methods for Cancer Detection using Augmented Datasets
summary: Cancer detection using AI methods and image databases faces several challenges, including limited and imbalanced image datasets, long algorithm training times, and high-complexity feature generation. In particular, many cancer image datasets contain very few malignant examples compared to benign ones, limiting the amount of minority-class data available for training. Although classical AI and especially deep learning methods have had some success in providing cancer diagnostics, Quantum Machine Learning (QML) methods may offer advantages through high-dimensional feature representations, generative data augmentation, and the exploitation of feature correlations through quantum properties such as entanglement. In this paper, we propose using a generative QML method on the compressed breast ultrasound image dataset (BUSI) to generate synthetic images and hence augmented datasets for classifier training. In particular, we train a convolutional neural network with real, synthetic, and a combination of real and synthetic images. We test the algorithm on real images and provide comparative results for all three training cases. Our results show that the classifier trained entirely on synthetic images achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.802 (80.2%), compared with 0.760 (76.0%) for the real-data baseline.

title: Shifted-Chart Composition for Horizon-Optimal Time-Varying LQR
comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to the 2027 American Control Conference (ACC); under review
summary: Horizon optimization in finite-horizon LQR treats the horizon $T$ as a decision variable and adds a penalty $wT$ to the cost. Recent composition-based methods evaluate all candidate horizons in $O(Nn^3)$, instead of the $O(N^2n^3)$ of one Riccati recursion per horizon, but they track the inverse cost-to-go $P^{-1}$ and therefore require every stage and terminal cost to be positive definite, whereas LQR requires only positive semidefiniteness. This excludes costs that leave some states unpenalized. In this work, we track instead the shifted inverse $\widehat{P}_k=(P_k+cI)^{-1}$, the inverse coordinate after a symplectic shear of the state-costate variables. Its domain contains every positive semidefinite Riccati matrix, and $P_k=\widehat{P}_k^{-1}-cI$ recovers the Riccati solution. We show that the shift can be absorbed into the stage coefficients of the inverse-coordinate composition, so the $O(Nn^3)$ search carries over, exact in exact arithmetic, subject to invertibility conditions. These hold for all small $c$ when the dynamics contract the unpenalized directions, fail for at most finitely many $c$ outside a degenerate case, and are certified per horizon at run time. In our experiments, diagonal loading $Q_k+\varepsilon I$ either left cost errors several orders of magnitude above those of the shifted chart or, for small fixed $\varepsilon$, selected the wrong horizon. The shifted chart with a fixed default $c$ selected the correct horizon on all tested instances, reporting long horizons as uncertified in one stress case.

title: From bits to atoms: A survey of cross-layer safety in Embodied AI
comment: Review article published in AI Plus. 25 pages, 6 figures. URL: https://www.the-innovation.org/ai-plus/article/doi/10.59717/ipj.aiplus.2026.100013
summary: Embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) introduces cyber-physical risks because digital failures and attacks can cause physical harm. This survey organizes embodied AI safety through a four-layer reference architecture -- comprising the physical interaction, system and middleware, algorithm and decision, and cloud-edge and data layers -- and uses it to connect vulnerabilities, propagation paths, and safeguards across the system stack. It traces the evolution of safety paradigms and examines how faults and attacks cross architectural boundaries to produce physical consequences. Furthermore, the survey systematizes composite attack chains, outlines multi-layered defense strategies, and reviews representative embodied safety benchmarks. Ultimately, we advocate for unifying software alignment with rigorous hardware constraints to build trustworthy systems capable of operating safely within human-centric environments.

title: TrajCFG: Token-Wise Classifier-Free Guidance via Denoising Trajectory Feedback
summary: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) typically applies a shared scale to all latent tokens, although their velocity predictions evolve differently during sampling. We introduce Trajectory-Adaptive Classifier-Free Guidance (TrajCFG), a training-free method for flow-matching models that adapts token-wise guidance using historical changes in guided velocity direction. TrajCFG maps this feedback to bounded scales, assigning stronger guidance to larger directional changes and weaker guidance to more consistent directions. It combines adjacent-step and interval-normalized longer-span feedback, reusing standard CFG predictions without additional model evaluations. Controlled diagnostics and ablations examine the roles of directional feedback, token-wise allocation, and history-span fusion. Experiments on text-to-video, image-to-video, text-to-audio-video, text-to-image, and image-to-3D generation show improvements over base samplers across multiple backbones. For text-to-video generation, TrajCFG improves VBench Total scores by 0.30-0.75 points over the strongest evaluated baseline on each of three backbones. These results support historical directional feedback as a broadly applicable signal for fine-grained guidance allocation. The project page is available at https://jyliu-98.github.io/trajcfg-project-page/.

title: Next-Concept Modeling: Fast, Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation
summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) offer parallel sampling for faster generation than autoregressive models, an increasingly important advantage as inference becomes a dominant computational workload. However, DLMs degrade quickly with fewer sampling steps, process the full sequence at every step, and require many passes over the dataset to reach good quality. We introduce Next-Concept Modeling (NCM), a two-stage, coarse-to-fine framework: a multiscale residual VQ-VAE encodes text into a hierarchy of discrete codes, and a transformer generates one level at a time, predicting all codes within a level in parallel. At matched parameter scales, NCM achieves better generative perplexity than the strongest DLM baseline on LM1B while running $21\times$ faster. On OpenWebText, NCM is competitive with the strongest DLM while running $10\times$ faster; on XSum, it matches the strongest DLM's ROUGE-L while being $31\times$ faster. On the reasoning task of Sudoku, NCM outperforms autoregressive and diffusion baselines across all difficulty levels, using fewer function evaluations. On the reasoning task of Sudoku, NCM outperforms autoregressive and diffusion baselines across all difficulty levels, using fewer function evaluations.

title: Hybrid Context Forests and Bilateral Viterbi Matching for 3D Rib Centerline Tracing in CT
summary:
Automatic extraction and anatomical numbering (R01-R12, L01-L12) of all 24 rib centerlines in thoracic CT is essential for unfolded rib visualization, fracture detection, and surgical navigation, but remains challenging due to adjacent-bone confluence, calcified costal cartilage bridges, kyphotic pose variation, and partial visibility of terminal ribs. We present ribline, an open-source three-stage framework combining: (1) an automatically detected lung-apex and vertebral-midline coordinate frame with a kyphosis-aware azimuthal angle for point ordering along each rib; (2) a hybrid voxel detector fusing an anatomically anchored Semantic Context Forest (SCF) with a lightweight 3D U-Net; and (3) a global stage that decomposes the probability skeleton into candidate curves, assigns rib indices via a bilateral Viterbi dynamic program coupled across both hemithoraces, and refines curves via template recovery and normal-plane centering (RibSnake). On the Siemens Corporate Research 2 mm thoracic CT benchmark (47 training and 12 evaluation scans), our pipeline achieves a labeled Chamfer distance of 2.05 mm, labeled clDice of 0.886 (3 mm) and 0.945 (4 mm), 97.2% labeling accuracy (278/286 ribs), and zero false-positive curves on the evaluation split, and 3.64 mm (median 2.39 mm) with 91.8% labeling accuracy across all 59 annotated scans (1,402 ribs) in 5-fold cross-validation.
  Code: https://github.com/wq2012/ribline
  Pretrained Models: https://huggingface.co/collections/wq2012/ribline

title: Defending Consensus-Based Cooperative Sensing Against Conformity-Driven Byzantine Attacks in 6G UAV Swarm Networks
summary: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enabled six-generation (6G) networks, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms increasingly rely on consensus-based cooperative sensing: each node iteratively exchanges and fuses decisions with its neighbors to approach a global picture of the environment, supporting the high-reliability, low-latency inference demanded by mission-critical tasks. Yet this very mechanism of conformity becomes the lever of Byzantine attacks. By exploiting the update rule, malicious nodes manufacture a false consensus that lures honest nodes into drifting away from their true observations round after round, so that a normal node's actual error probability evolves dynamically and rises far above its intrinsic sensing error. Conventional fusion models, which assume node errors are fixed and independent, are therefore severely mismatched. This article argues for a different defensive perspective: instead of hunting for bad nodes, we seek to understand how good nodes turn bad, characterizing the inducement dynamics with evolutionary game theory and handing this law to the fusion center so that it can dynamically correct the true error level of normal nodes. Simulations show that the approach sustains near-perfect situational inference across a wide range of attack intensities and network sizes, while naturally supporting low latency decisions. We further discuss several open challenges on the path toward secure ISAC-6G swarm sensing.

title: RAIN: Robotic Task Generalization with Region-Aware Interaction Networks
summary: Existing vision-language-action (VLA) models benefit from large-scale vision-language pretraining, but tend to memorize training trajectories, limiting their ability to adapt learned interactions to new task and scene configurations. To address this problem, we propose \textbf{Region-Aware Interaction Networks (RAIN)}, which formulates a task as a sequence of goal-conditioned subtasks, each specified by an action type and a target-region mask. This formulation allows learned skills to be reused across different objects and scene layouts and composed into task sequences not seen during training. Its Target-adaptive Cross-View Encoder (TCE) conditions multi-view features on target masks and exchanges information across views, while PlanDiT predicts target-directed trajectories and actions. A Transition Head estimates subtask completion to enable automatic transitions. We also introduce a \textbf{Reference-based Retargeting Strategy (RRS)}, which uses recorded trajectories to synthesize smooth approaches to reference interactions with alternative target regions, without collecting additional data. Experiments on \textbf{LIBERO-Analogy}, our new benchmark for robotic task generalization, and real-world tabletop tasks demonstrate that RAIN generalizes more robustly than existing VLA baselines.

title: Video-Arena: A Scalable Agentic Video Benchmark for Spatiotemporal Capability
summary: Understanding and tracking a dynamic world are fundamental to visual intelligence. Existing video benchmarks provide limited insight into whether models can maintain a coherent understanding of evolving world state. Building such a benchmark from real-world videos is challenging because the underlying world state is partially observable, making annotations hard to obtain. To close this gap, we introduce Video-Arena, a benchmark that turns competitive games into scalable, verifiable tests of how well models understand evolving world states from videos. Specifically, inspired by how humans understand dynamic events, we evaluate spatiotemporal world state understanding and tracking through three task categories: perceiving critical events, interpreting state updates, and tracking the resulting states. Our pipeline can generate videos and aligned reference labels from game records at scale. To keep evaluation affordable and reproducible, we curate a golden set of 180 tasks across 9 games and run evaluations under two protocols: native visual understanding and tool-assisted agentic analysis. The best-performing systems achieve F1 scores of and under the two protocols, respectively. The result highlights that native models struggle to perceive events reliably, while tool-assisted systems improve event recovery but still struggle to interpret state updates and track the resulting states consistently over time. Our project page is in https://videoarena-bench.github.io

title: Modeling the Arrival Time of Information-Bearing Events in Natural Language
summary: Understanding how information is distributed over time is fundamental to modeling natural language. While existing empirical studies primarily rely on post-hoc analysis of information-theoretic metrics, such as surprisal, little is known about the generation processes under the surface. We propose a novel approach for addressing this gap using the tool of neural temporal point processes (TPPs) by modeling the key information-bearing events in text sequences with learnable event intensity functions. Our model takes the history of event intervals and the contextual semantic representations from LLMs as input, and predicts the future arrival times for two types of events: new-word and high-surprisal-token. The experimental results reveal an interesting distinction in event intensities: LLMs tend to produce new words at significantly higher rates than humans, while high-surprisal tokens do not exhibit the difference. A decaying pattern of intensity over time is found in new-word events for both humans and LLMs, but not in high-surprisal-token events. Our findings revisit and extend previous studies that use simpler methods; provide supplementary evidence for theories about constrained context representation inherent in human language production; and find a new angle to view human and LLM generation differences.

title: Artificiality's First Exam: An LLM-Referenced C-test for Supraintelligence
comment: Preprint, under review. 63 pages. Code and data at https://github.com/jorallo/ctest-one
summary: Under the accelerated pace of AI development, any benchmark whose difficulty is calibrated with humans or current AI systems becomes circular, or saturates soon. How can we then evaluate machines that may become more capable than the current machines and the people who write the tests? One answer to the question hinges on inverse problems, inductive inference questions for which difficulty depends on the complexity of the underlying mechanism, given the observations and the previous knowledge. Levin's Kt, a computable variant of Kolmogorov complexity, puts a theoretical upper bound to that difficulty, balancing the simplest representation encoding for the mechanism and the logarithm of the time steps to run that mechanism. Previous tests derived from Levin's Kt, such as the original C-test, are based on minimalistic Universal Turing Machines (UTM), capable of very limited representations and no previous knowledge. Reasoning large language models (LLM) are UTMs that capture a compendium of human culture as knowledge, using prompts as natural language programs. This paper presents the first test based on Levin's Kt with LLMs as representational machines. Fresh test items can be produced at high difficulties, estimated in a ratio scale measured in bits, before any human or frontier model can solve them. We formalise the measure, devise a lightweight generation and certification pipeline, explore the effect of the power of the reference machine and the gap between examiner and examinee. We produce a first battery of certified items administered to twelve LLMs. The resulting agent characteristic curves decrease with difficulty, down to the uncharted high-difficulty region, the supra-intelligence window of items we can certify, yet beyond generations of frontier intelligence.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Cortical Surface Reconstruction and Spherical Registration for Heterogeneous Brain MRI
summary: Surface-based cortical analysis is useful in many applications as it is a natural way to model the highly folded structure of the cerebral cortex, allowing quantities such as curvature and thickness to be easily calculated. Existing deep learning (DL) methods have focused on 1x1x1 mm3 T1-weighted (T1w) scans, thus replicating classical pipelines. Here we present a neural network that is trained exclusively on synthetic scans with random contrast and resolution. Consequently, it can be applied to almost any kind of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan. In addition, our model provides vertex-wise uncertainty estimates of the predicted surface as well as a spherical registration to fsaverage space. Our model performs on par with other state-of-the-art DL methods on 1x1x1 mm3 T1w scans and outperforms the only other method capable of estimating cortical surfaces from low resolution, non-T1w scans. The predicted uncertainty, moreover, correlates with overall scan quality on low resolution scans and highlights areas of poor surface reconstruction on 1x1x1 mm3 T1w scans, suggesting that it can be used for quality control. Finally, the predicted spherical registrations prove comparable to other DL and classical registration methods. These qualities, when combined with the fast inference time, will provide the ability to analyze large, existing databases of clinical MRI scans, with the potential for finding disease-specific patterns that would otherwise be infeasible in a research setting.

title: Decision-Focused Learning for Optimal Battery Scheduling Under Load and Photovoltaic Power Uncertainty in Microgrids
comment: 20 pages, 13 figures, submitted to Sustainable Energy, Grids and Networks
summary: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in microgrids demands accurate day-ahead forecasting to support optimal battery energy storage system (BESS) scheduling. Yet the conventional predict-then-optimize paradigm trains forecasters on statistical accuracy metrics that are agnostic to the asymmetric and time-varying cost impacts of forecast errors. This work proposes a decision-focused learning (DFL) framework that trains gated recurrent unit forecasters for both load demand and photovoltaic generation directly on the downstream operational cost of a two-stage energy management system, where day-ahead BESS commitments are fixed prior to real-time balancing. Gradients are backpropagated from the real-time operational cost through both optimization stages to the forecaster weights via implicit differentiation, enabling the forecasters to internalize the penalty structure of the scheduling problem. The framework is validated on the MG2Lab experimental microgrid testbed at Politecnico di Milano across two operational scenarios of increasing grid constraint and eight forecasting configurations comprising single-source and combined-forecaster settings. Results illustrate that the DFL-trained pipeline reduces operational cost by 3.78% under normal grid conditions and by 30.60% under grid-constrained conditions relative to the accuracy- optimized baseline, while nearly eliminating load shedding events. Notably, the DFL forecasters exhibit higher statistical errors than their accuracy-trained counterparts yet achieve consistently lower operational costs, confirming that forecast accuracy and decision quality do not share a monotonic relationship in constrained microgrid scheduling.

title: Reinforcement Learning from Real-Robot Interaction without High-Quality State Estimates
summary: A longstanding goal for robot reinforcement learning (RL) is that robots learn from their own physical experience, as humans and animals do. A key obstacle to learning directly from physical experience, especially outside instrumented lab environments, is that the state of the world is usually unobservable to the learner and must be estimated from on-board sensing. Errors in that estimate corrupt both the policy input and potentially the reward signal. We study this challenge using the contact-rich task of a bipedal robot learning to score soccer goals. We estimate all key state variables on-board with an unscented Kalman filter (UKF) and no external instrumentation (e.g., motion capture or overhead cameras). Because the UKF may incorrectly estimate state when the ball is unobserved, we learn a new state representation with a recurrent state-space model (RSSM) that, critically, only corrects the RSSM's latent state when the ball is observed. Building on RLPD, we introduce RSSM-RLPD and apply it to the task of a NAO robot learning to dribble a soccer ball into a goal. We show that the robot learns to score from multiple starting positions after 30 minutes of real-world interaction, reaching 100% success against 0% for a feed-forward policy under the same training budget. We complement our physical robot experiments with a simulation study and show that RSSM-RLPD learns policies that achieve a higher success rate than behavior cloning, a feed-forward, and GRU baseline. Taken together, our results show that the addition of a learned state representation to existing on-robot learning methods enables RL from real-robot data even with a high degree of partial observability.

title: Token-Budgeted Candidate Retrieval for 3D Scene-Grounded VLMs: Category Names vs. Pairwise Geometry
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Physical World AI (non-archival)
summary: Under a fixed context budget, which objects and relations should a 3D scene-grounded VLM see first? On ScanNet indoor referring benchmarks (Dai et al., 2017), matching the query to object category names outperforms pairwise geometry scoring at every reported K. The gaps are largest at high recall. Analytic pairwise cues beat per-object cue scoring and query-agnostic kNN graphs, including on paraphrases. MiniLM and BGE-small still score higher on those splits. We evaluate token-budgeted candidate retrieval with axis-aligned boxes, a token-ratio metric, training-free baselines, two small encoders that match q to each object's category name, and QCRR (Query-Conditioned Relation Retrieval), a deterministic pairwise-geometry scorer. Across ScanRefer gt_val plus a custom 20% scan-id split of Nr3D and Sr3D (35,504 queries; not official ReferIt3D val), additive noun matching reaches R@10 0.864 on ScanRefer against QCRR's 0.626; MiniLM and BGE-small reach 0.911 to 0.913 on ScanRefer and 0.941 to 0.947 on Nr3D. A corrected 3DGraphLLM harness (native Acc@0.25 0.67 on the full graph, n=300 ScanRefer queries) shows that context selection changes downstream accuracy under a matched object budget (Random 0.44, QCRR 0.56, MiniLM 0.67, oracle 0.70). Semantic retrieval beats hand-designed geometry on that harness. We will release the protocol, retriever implementations, and per-query outputs so new selectors can be swapped in without rewriting the analysis.

title: Agentic Data Engineering for LLMs: System Design and a Controlled Empirical Study
summary: LLM data engineering requires iterative experimentation to determine how data selection, rewards, and curricula affect model learning, making it a natural setting for AI-for-AI (AI4AI) research. Can agents use experimental feedback to progressively improve strategies, and do the resulting strategies improve target-model performance on held-out data? We study how agents use experimental feedback to develop data-engineering strategies under fixed training and evaluation protocols. Our Agentic Data Engineering (ADE) framework lets agents pursue, revise, or combine research directions using cumulative findings. Strategies are selected by in-loop scores and evaluated on held-out benchmarks. Across four tasks-math and code data selection, math reward design, and math curriculum learning-selected strategies achieve absolute gains over generic baselines of up to 13.34% on AIME25 Pass@32 and 5.85% averaged across four held-out benchmarks under fixed training conditions. In-loop scores improve over successive experiments, while held-out trajectories show that later in-loop gains do not always improve generalization. Comparisons of research organization and feedback access favor combining evidence analysis with cumulative findings. Research trajectories show how earlier findings inform strategy revisions and combinations across research directions.

title: The Silent Failures in Agentic Data Science
summary: Large language models have significantly lowered the barrier to writing code. Naturally, this has also led to the development of data science agents that promise automating the design and execution of data science from task formulation to model development. Existing evaluations of agentic data science (agentic DS) assess downstream predictive performance and code correctness, providing preliminary insight in agentic DS capabilities. We argue that these evaluations overlook the fundamental principles of data science: methodological data science- and domain knowledge. As such, only assessing downstream performance masks methodological failures such as data leakage and inappropriate validation, limiting the development of robust agentic DS systems. In this paper, we evaluate agentic DS beyond accuracy from three different angles: 1) a large-scale analysis of failure modes in common agentic DS frameworks and models across 220 data science tasks, 2) a reusable and extensible test suite with curated data science tasks that test for six specific failures in a controlled manner, and 3) a qualitative assessment of agentic DS pipelines against expert solutions on Kaggle competitions. We find that the majority of agentic solutions contain at least one failure mode despite the complexity of agentic harness or model capacity. Moreover, we identify a positive correlation between the occurrence of data leakage failures and predictive performance, confirming the necessity to evaluate agents beyond accuracy. Our qualitative analysis shows that DS agents generally lack problem solving creativity and domain knowledge, compared to competition-winning data scientists. We believe that principled failure mode analysis, as presented here, should be integral part of agentic DS evaluations, and that the insights we surface will be key in developing trustworthy agentic DS pipelines.

title: Calibrating Generative Flows through Regional Probability Matching
summary: Generative models offer a powerful route to scientific simulation and discovery by enabling the study of complex populations and rare phenomena. Flow matching can generate realistic samples, yet inaccurate occurrence frequencies can distort population statistics and compromise inferences about rare events. Here we developed generalized mass-preserving coupled flow matching (G-MPCF), which matches the probability masses of Gaussian source regions to those of weighted data regions. This construction encodes the desired regional frequencies in the correspondence between noise and observations, shaping the learned dynamics while preserving the prescribed target distribution. On a rare-mode benchmark, G-MPCF reduces relative score error by 95.0% and numerical integration error by 89.9% compared with independent flow matching. On CIFAR-10 with a 100:1 class-probability ratio, it reduces corrected class-mass error by 44.6% compared with minibatch optimal transport, while improving mean image fidelity with matched computational budgets. We envision that incorporating regional probability calibration into generative modelling will support more reliable scientific simulation and inference, enabling the study of systems in which rare events and their occurrence frequencies are central to understanding the underlying mechanisms.

title: An Adaptive Cyber-Resilient Framework for P2P Energy Trading under Optimal Stealthy Attacks
summary: The increasing adoption of peer to peer energy trading has enabled prosumers to actively participate in decentralized energy markets. However, the growing dependence of P2P energy markets on communication infrastructures and distributed coordination mechanisms introduces an expanded cyberattack surface, enabling sophisticated adversaries to manipulate market interactions while remaining concealed from conventional detection mechanisms. This paper first designs an optimal stealthy attack that maximizes economic disruption of the MicroGrids, while preserving the apparent convergence characteristics of the ADMM based market-clearing process. To detect such attacks, a Mahalanobis Boosting detector is developed using market layer features to effectively capture inter feature dependencies and distinguish compromised updates from normal market operation. An adaptive rho based mitigation strategy is then introduced to limit the propagation of compromised information and restore robust market operation once an attack is flagged. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through comprehensive case studies, achieving an attack detection accuracy of 98.49% while the proposed mitigation strategy reduces the operating cost by approximately 18.43% compared to the unmitigated attack case. The proposed approach provides a practical pathway toward trustworthy and cyber-secure distributed P2P energy trading systems.

title: Terrain Traversal Without Motion Priors: Expert-Routed Humanoid Locomotion at Deployment Fidelity
summary: State-of-the-art perceptive humanoid locomotion is mostly built on retargeted motion capture, a generative motion prior, and a distillation stage. We report a complete system that does not require this pipeline for a humanoid to cross varied terrain. In its place, we provide a five-expert mixture routed by a terrain classifier over a sensed elevation grid, and target every foothold with a model-based planner, refined by six closed-form-gradient steps on an interpolated terrain-cost field instead of picked from a fixed grid. Driven through the same perception-to-actuation software a robot would run, inside a second, deployment-fidelity simulator, it crosses an $85$\,m five-segment waypoint course $18$ of $20$ times end-to-end ($90\%$, Wilson $95\%$ CI $70$--$97$) and succeeds $20/20$ on four of five segments scored alone, where an ablated configuration without the mixture and without refinement reaches $0\%$ on both the stair and the hurdle segment. The continuous refinement moves $72.4\%$ of foot placements across at least one grid-cell boundary, which produces real sub-grid correction. We also ran matched component studies to report what does not account for it: one expert equals five on the training distribution, four label-free routers collapse to near-uniform activation, and a self-supervised terrain embedding loses to the privileged label.

title: CAPTOR: a vision-language foundation model for Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis Oncologic CT
summary:
Purpose : To develop and evaluate CAPTOR, a deep-learning vision-language foundation model for oncologic chest-abdomen-pelvis (CAP) CT interpretation.
  Materials & Methods : CAPTOR (Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis foundaTion model for Oncologic Radiology) is a contrastive vision-language model, trained using a pretraining strategy for oncologic CAP CT (in single- or multiple-series acquisitions), on a multicenter retrospective dataset from North America, Europe and Asia, predominantly from tumor lesion examinations. CAPTOR was compared with state-of-the-art CT foundation models on three downstream tasks: disease detection, survival prediction using TumorImagingBench and image retrieval. Classification and retrieval were both evaluated on held-out internal and public test sets, stratified by anatomical coverage and indication. Bootstrap resampling was used to estimate confidence intervals, and pairwise comparisons were performed using permutation tests.
  Results : CAPTOR was trained and tested on 25,512 and 10,794 CT-report pairs respectively. TumorImagingBench datasets comprised between 134 and 421 studies each. CAPTOR outperformed all baseline models, on the classification task, on the CAP subset (AUC 0.767, 95%CI: 0.734-0.793, vs. 0.695, 95%CI: 0.645-0.736 for the next-best, p<0.001) and oncologic subset (AUC 0.784, 95%CI: 0.759-0.805, vs. 0.734, 95%CI: 0.703-0.767 p<0.001), ranked first on three of the four oncologic prognostic benchmarks, and achieved superior retrieval performance on CAP and oncologic subsets.
  Conclusion : A foundation model trained on oncology-enriched CAP CT data outperformed relevant state-of-the-art models in its target clinical context, underscoring the importance of clinically aligned pretraining.
  We release our preprocessing, training and inference code : https://github.com/Guerbet-AI/CAPTOR and model weights : https://huggingface.co/Guerbet-AI/CAPTOR

title: The Thinking Leakage in Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
summary: Hybrid reasoning models such as the Qwen3 series switch between a THINK mode and a NO-THINK mode through a few chat-template tokens. A popular recipe trains such models with reinforcement learning in NO-THINK mode and reports improved reasoning performance. We provide evidence that much of this gain can be explained by thinking leakage: the gain comes largely from partially reactivating the reasoning abilities of the original model's THINK mode instead of learning enhanced reasoning behavior. We train Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B with GRPO in NO-THINK mode. As accuracy improves, responses become longer and more reflective, are increasingly judged by the original model to resemble its own thinking, and the model's internal activations shift toward its THINK mode. We then investigate at the level of weights, activations, and attention heads: scaling the RL update further elicits THINK-mode behavior and approaches THINK-mode accuracy but does not exceed it; in Qwen3-8B, replacing a low-dimensional THINK-related activation subspace of the RL-trained model with its original-model value removes most of the RL gain, and the reverse exchange transfers a considerable fraction of the gain to the original model; and the RL-induced shift passes through the attention heads that read the empty think block. We further identify a possible mechanism in the GRPO training signal: responses favored by the advantage-weighted update are more THINK-like, and a gradient step computed from this signal moves the model toward its THINK state. Thus, gains in NO-THINK mode can largely reflect reactivation of reasoning abilities already present in the original model.

title: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop
